what_this_is: A capability id -> (module, verifier) binding that lets the runtime resolve a capability BY NAME without the front door importing it. A declared capability is reachable; that is not the same as being correct, scored, or credited. Every entry additionally requires: the module exists, the verifier exists, and the verifier is itself reachable.
why_it_exists: A reachability census found 1,639 of 2,247 canonical/runtime modules unreachable from brain_unified_model_v1. Several of the most load-bearing ones -- the zero-model SWE agent, the OSWorld task-state ledger, aimed selection -- were unreachable while having passing test suites. A module that no entry point can reach cannot participate in a solve, however good it is. Declaration is the minimum repair: it makes the module addressable without editing the import graph, and it forces each binding to name the check that would falsify it.
admission_rule: module path must exist in the tree at this commit
verifier path must exist and must itself be reachable from a front door
preconditions and effects are stated, even when empty, so a router can read them
an entry whose verifier is missing is reported as defective and grants nothing
known_defects: verifier_falsification_v1: 1,637 lines, 76KB, no test file, orphaned. It is the module whose whole premise is 'a check that cannot fail is not a check'. It cannot currently be run by anything. Not declared here: a verifier that does not exist as a runnable check cannot be the verifier of a declared capability.
